newsitem.title: USA: Most IMM currencies end higher,led by stg, Aus dlr.
newsitem.headline: Most IMM currencies end higher,led by stg, Aus dlr.

text.p: IMM currency futures finished mostly higher, with strong gains in Australian dollars and sterling dominating activity, traders and analysts said.
"There are a lot of funds looking for high-yielders," one cash trader said.
They said the rally in December Australian dollars was technically driven, as the contract shot through $0.08050 on GLOBEX.
December Australian dollars closed at a record high of $0.8118, as one major U.S. fund was reportedly bidding late in the day for $200 million Austrlian in the cash market.
This fund has bought an estimated $300 million Australian dollars in the last two days, he said.
"The buying in Australian dollars has been absolutely huge," another trader said.

Traders in both futures and cash currency markets said the demand for sterling was still strong as retail funds found themselves short the currency. One cash trader at a major European bank said there was still anecdotal evidence that U.K. manufacturers and exporters were short sterling.
They said profit-taking might emerge as December approaches $1.70. December set a contract high of $1.6904 on Thursday.
One technical analyst said resistance is at $1.6930, a multi-year high.
"Sterling is due for a 200-point pullback, but bids should emerge," another trader said. "There are some major institutions that are short."

Meanwhile, cash sterling/mark rose above 2.53 to a high last seen in April 1994. The cash cross rate may find some resistance at 2.5385, a congestion area, and at the 72-month moving average of 2.5430.
"If you get through there you may have to project a rise to 2.55," he said.
He said sterling/mark was vulnerable to a selloff if the mark starts to strengthen against the dollar. Currently, the dollar's outlook has been overshadowed by cross trade.
While marks fell against sterling, the currency stabilized against the yen, rose against the French franc and recovered against the Italian lira and peseta.

The conter-cross activity should keep December marks range-bound, and trading below $0.6700, or 1.4950 spot. December marks could rise to $0.6744 at the most, as foreign institutions are reportedly short at 1.4850 spot.

At the end of pit trade, December yen was up $0.000020 at $0.009011, marks were down $0.0004 at $0.6686, Swiss francs were steady at $0.7915, sterling was up $0.0090 at $1.6886, Canadian dollars were up $0.0002 at $0.7481, Australian dollars rose $0.0108 at $0.8118 and Mexican pesos were up $0.000450 at $0.125000. -Derivatives desk 312-408-8750;E-mail derivatives@reuters.com
